title: Structure-based classification of hormones
guide: Amino-acid derivatives: tyrosine → T3/T4 and catecholamines (adrenaline 80%, noradrenaline, dopamine); tryptophan → serotonin, melatonin. Vitamin derivatives: A and D. Peptides: small (<50 AA) = ACTH, ADH, oxytocin, all hypothalamic; large (>50 AA) = GH 191, prolactin 199, insulin 51, PTH, renin; glycoproteins (protein > carbohydrate) = FSH/LH/TSH, >200 AA with common α subunit. Steroids: glomerulosa aldosterone, fasciculata cortisol, reticularis DHEAS/androstenedione; sex hormones estrogen/progesterone/testosterone. DHEAS = most abundant adreno-cortical hormone in fetal life.

title: Tryptophan derivatives, sleep–wake cycle and the 80/20 rules
guide: Serotonin (enterochromaffin cells of GIT) keeps us alert; melatonin (pineal) aids sleep. Morning light → retinal ganglion cells → raphe nuclei → serotonin; night (9:30–10 pm) serotonin falls and melatonin rises to a 2–2:30 am peak. Night gadget overuse → serotonin stays up → melatonin cannot rise → disrupted sleep–wake → depression. Happiness hormones DOSE. Adrenal 80/20: cortex/medulla; medulla 80% adrenaline/20% noradrenaline.

title: Mechanism-based classification and Group I (nuclear) hormones
guide: Group I: intracellular receptor, lipophilic, carrier protein (+), long t½; act via gene transcription >> transport channels. Type I/homodimer = cytoplasm, steroids; Type 2/heterodimer = nucleus, T3/T4/vitamin A&D. Steroid receptor held inactive by Hsp-90; hormone binding releases Hsp-90 and the R–H complex binds GREs.

title: Type II nuclear receptors, orphan receptors and PPAR agonists
guide: VDR (calcitriol = 1,25(OH)2D3) heterodimerizes with RXR and binds VDREs; TR on TRE sheds co-repressor and recruits co-activator on T3 binding. Homodimers = steroid receptors; heterodimers = TR, VDR, RAR, PPAR; orphans (no ligand) = SF1, DAX1 (gonadotrophs + adrenal cortex) and HNF4α (defect → MODY type 1). PPARα clofibrate (TG >440 mg/dL); PPARγ pioglitazone (insulin resistance; risks salt-water retention, fractures, bladder cancer); dual saroglitazar (DOC diabetic dyslipidaemia, NAFLD, NASH). Metformin also combats insulin resistance.

title: Group II hormones: second messengers and the GPCR cycle
guide: Group II act through second messengers on transport channels, translation, modification and transcription. Receptor types: GPCR, TKR, JAK/cytokine, STKR. GPCR: hormone → GDP→GTP on α, α dissociates to the effector. Gs/Gi → cAMP → PKA → phosphorylation; Gq → PLC on PIP2 → DAG (PKC) + IP3 (Ca2+/calmodulin); Gt = transducin (cAMP).

title: The GPCR hormone map, cGMP vasodilators and TKR
guide: cAMP users: CRH; ACTH/FSH/LH/TSH; V2; β and α2 (Gi); secretin/glucagon/somatostatin (Gi); PTH/calcitonin. IP3/DAG users: TRH/GnRH; V1/V3/oxytocin; AT II/substance P; α1/ACh; CCK/gastrin. Gi lowers cAMP. cGMP vasodilators: NO and ANF; urotensin = most potent vasoconstrictor. TKR: ligand → dimerisation → autophosphorylation; insulin → PI3K/Akt → GLUT4 (adipose, skeletal muscle, heart); growth factors all use TKR except TGF β.

title: JAK–STAT and serine–threonine kinase receptors
guide: JAK–STAT: ligand → dimerisation → STAT phosphorylation → transcription; users GH, prolactin (twin hormones), EPO; JAK2 mutations in PRV, primary myelofibrosis, essential thrombocytosis. STKR phosphorylates SMAD; users activin, inhibin, BMP, TGF-β (most potent pathogenic fibrogenic cytokine, 'stroke master').
